decision.question: How does the page.jsonl code join Page with the fewest lines in Page.class.js?
decision.chose: core/Page/Log.js exports class PageLog; Page extends PageLog (one import, one word, one super() call)
over: copying methods onto Page.prototype with a mixin helper
decision.why: Inheritance is plain to read and the statics come with it, so Card.jsonl(url) builds a Card with nothing extra. A mixin would be hidden wiring, and inline code would make Page.class.js longer.

decision.question: How does {"file": "x", "gone": true} reach the file entry when set() passes each method exactly one argument?
decision.chose: gone(true) is its own method: set() calls file("x") first, then gone(true), which removes the file that was just named
decision.why: It keeps the one-argument rule and needs no mapping table. It also matches the watcher's line shape exactly.

decision.question: A Map also has set(), which takes two arguments. What happens to a line key that names children?
decision.chose: set() skips a key whose current value is a Map: it never passes the value down and never replaces it
over: passing the value to Map.set, which would store it as a key with no value
replacing the Map, which would break the page
decision.why: children is core's own bookkeeping. The page.jsonl way to add a child is a file line.
